USDA Crop Progress (delayed by Columbus Day)

outlook: Grains were lower in overnight trade Tuesday after a mixed Monday close, when December corn recovered 3¼ cents to $4.83 following Friday's post-WASDE sell-off and November soybeans slipped 3¾ cents. Overnight, December corn was down 1½ cents and November soybeans down 4¾ cents, as traders wait for China to resume significant U.S. purchases after its national holiday and Brazil's soybean planting runs a record-fast 20% complete. Wheat was lower across the board, with Minneapolis spring wheat off 1½ cents, after a U.S. dollar at an 18-month high pressured prices Monday; IKAR trimmed its Russian wheat crop estimate to 88.0 million tonnes. ICE canola reopened after Canadian Thanksgiving up about C$2.70, and USDA's delayed Crop Progress report is due at 3 pm CT today with strong harvest progress expected.
